title: eludite.forge.pull_review input
description: Review a pull request: `start` opens a pending review, `add` adds a comment on `path` and `line` to it (pending), `submit` submits it with `event` `approve`, `request_changes` or `comment` and an optional `body` (Azure DevOps: a vote; GitLab: `approve` approves and the comments are a batch of draft notes), `discard` drops the pending review, `request` asks the `reviewers` (default the previous reviewers) to review again. Where the forge has no pending reviews, `add` posts the comment at once and `submit` posts the summary. For an agent, under the solution policy's `forge.write`: `prompt` (the default) makes the first write of an agent session dangerous (the Agents window asks; "Allow for this session" holds until the session ends), `allow` runs it, `deny` refuses it. The repository is the workspace's (its remote `origin`, or `remote`), detected as eludite.forge.detect does; every call runs on the forge worker off the UI thread with a timeout and stops when canceled. A call that needs a token when none is stored for the host fails with `sign_in_required: <host>`: the person signs in (Git > Sign in to <forge>); an agent cannot.
x-eludite-escalates: Execute; For an agent, under the solution policy's `forge.write`: `prompt` (the default) makes the first write of an agent session dangerous (the Agents window asks; "Allow for this session" holds until the session ends), `allow` runs it, `deny` refuses it.

number.description: The number (GitHub, GitLab's `iid`, Azure DevOps, Forgejo, Gitea). Give `number` or `id`.

id.description: The item's `id` as a list answered it; Tangled's items have only this (their AT-URI). Give `number` or `id`.

remote.description: The git remote to read (default `origin`, else the only remote).

items.description: A user's login (user name) on the forge; on Tangled their handle, else their DID.
